subject: Zip supplier portal invite failing due to origin header validation
messages:
From: Sara Klein <s.klein@zipvendor.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2026 09:18:12 -0700
Subject: Zip invite failing - origin header rejection

Hi Jasmine,

Quick flag from our onboarding team — the supplier (EverCraft Supplies) reports the invite link you sent results in an authentication error when they click Accept: the browser console and our gateway show an Origin header mismatch and the POST is rejected (401). I attached the invite-request.log excerpt that shows: 

  > 2026-06-10T16:14:05Z POST /api/invite 401 origin: https://portal.zipvendor.com
  > expected origins: [https://zipportal.zipvendor.com]

They are able to access other links on the same domain but the invite flow calls back to our invite endpoint which appears to validate Origin strictly. Can you confirm what host/redirection your invite uses, and whether Redwood can set a fallback?

Attaching: invite-request.log (small)

Thanks,
Sara Klein
Onboarding Manager
ZipVendor, Inc.

Attachments: invite-request.log (text)
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Sara Klein <s.klein@zipvendor.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2026 10:03:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Zip invite failing - origin header rejection

Thanks for the heads up, Sara — I pulled the log and reproduced the failure with a test invite. Quick summary and proposed next steps: 

What I see:
- Your gateway is validating the Origin header against an allowlist (strict match).
- Our invite redirect goes to https://portal.zipvendor.com/accept?token=... while the service that validates expects https://zipportal.zipvendor.com (subdomain mismatch).
- When Origin doesn't match the allowlist the request is rejected early (401).

Short-term options:
1) Zip temporarily add https://portal.zipvendor.com to the allowlist for invite endpoints so existing tokens can be accepted while we reconcile hostnames.
2) We can issue a new invite link that uses the canonical host (zipportal.zipvendor.com) — I can re-send from the console if you prefer.
3) If neither is possible, our platform can create a one-off fallback link that disables Origin validation for that token only (requires sign-off from your security team).

I've attached a screenshot of the error from the browser and a quick gateway snippet. Ben — tagging you for a possible gateway rewrite suggestion (we saw an X-Forwarded-Host rewrite pattern in our infra that might address this without changing tokens).

Can you share which of the three you'd prefer? If Zip can do the allowlist change, that will be fastest. If you want us to regenerate invites, tell me which supplier emails should be reissued and I'll queue them.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com
(Attachment: portal-error-screenshot.png)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Sara Klein <s.klein@zipvendor.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2026 11:22:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Zip invite failing - origin header rejection

Good morning — jumping in with a technical note. We saw this pattern before when a customer fronted the invite service with an internal proxy that rewrites host/origin values. A couple of practical fixes: 

- Best: Zip adds the portal alias (https://portal.zipvendor.com) to the invite endpoint allowlist for the short window while we reconcile DNS/SNI. This is quick and low-risk.
- If your security policy disallows adding aliases, we can emit a new invite with the canonical host. That avoids any server-side config changes.
- For a minimal infra change on our side, we can have our gateway send a redirect to the canonical host rather than proxy the POST; that avoids Origin being sent in the validation check. This requires a short deploy (we can ship a patch to the invite handler in the next sprint).

I've attached a gateway-log-snippet showing the Host/Origin pairs we observed and a sample cURL that reproduces the reject.

Jasmine — if you re-issue invites via the console, please include a note to suppliers to clear caches or use an incognito window (we saw one client with a cached service worker that held an old base URL).

Ben Carter
Senior Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: gateway-log-snippet.txt)
From: Sara Klein <s.klein@zipvendor.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2026 15:05:50 -0700
Subject: Re: Zip invite failing - origin header rejection

Thanks, all — internal engineering just confirmed they'll add https://portal.zipvendor.com to the allowlist for the invite endpoints and will redeploy in the next hour.

We'll validate against the supplier (EverCraft) once it's live and let you know. If the allowlist change doesn't clear the case, we'll ask you to reissue the invites and will include your suggested note about cache/workarounds.

I've also uploaded an updated invite (different hostname) to our onboarding bucket; link is attached.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Sara
Attachments: zip-updated-invite.html
